exchange.text:
**Takeaway:** AMD's operating margin turned negative in fiscal Q2 2025 (period ending June 2025) because gross margin collapsed, and management attributed the deterioration to U.S. export controls on Instinct MI308 data center GPUs that triggered roughly $800 million in inventory and related charges.

**Trend across the window shown:** AMD's operating margin held in a narrow band from fiscal Q3 2024 (period ending September 2024) through fiscal Q1 2025 (period ending March 2025)—10.6%, 11.4%, and 10.8% respectively—then plunged to -1.7% in fiscal Q2 2025 (period ending June 2025). It recovered immediately to 13.7% in fiscal Q3 2025 (period ending September 2025) and continued edging higher through fiscal Q2 2026 (period ending June 2026), reaching 14.4%. Gross margin followed the same pattern: stable near 50–51%, a drop to 39.8% in fiscal Q2 2025, then a rebound to 53.6% and a plateau around 54%.

**What is strong and what is weak:** The fiscal Q2 2025 quarter is the clear outlier in every profitability metric shown. AMD's gross margin of 39.8% (F20) is the lowest in the entire eight-quarter window, and AMD's operating margin of -1.7% (F28) is the only negative reading. Revenue of $7.7B (F12) was not the problem—it was flat with fiscal Q4 2024 and up modestly quarter-over-quarter. The weakness was entirely in cost of goods or charges hitting gross profit.

**Counterpoint:** Despite the negative operating margin, AMD reported net income of $872.0M (F4) and a net margin of 11.3% (F7) for fiscal Q2 2025 (period ending June 2025), meaning below-the-line items more than offset the operating loss. The operating-margin headline overstates the bottom-line damage in that quarter.

**What the data cannot tell:** The figures shown do not break out operating expenses separately from cost of goods sold, so we cannot see how much of the gross-margin decline came from the inventory charge versus other COGS items. There is also no prior-year fiscal Q2 revenue or margin for a year-over-year comparison.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** The $800 million charge may have been split between cost of goods sold and operating expenses, given that AMD's gross margin fell by more than the operating margin implies when compared to the prior quarter's spread between the two.

Management attribution (from a claim published August 2025): AMD stated that U.S. Government export controls on Instinct MI308 data center GPU products led to approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the quarter.
